urn:eigenius:core:description: A user-authored Lean Lake project — the directory tree the authoring side stages into a `LeanEnvironment` image for `lean_export` / `dispatch_method` invocation. Inherits the `RuntimePackage` shape (name + manifest + source_tree + `language: lean`) and adds the two Lake-specific artefacts: `lakefile.lean` and `lake-manifest.json`. The 20a.5b worker treats this as the input shape for the `lean_export` RPC verb.

Verbatim `lakefile.lean` content as a UTF-8 string. The substrate image-build pipeline writes this to disk inside the package's directory in the build context; `lake update` reads it to resolve dependencies.

Verbatim `lake-manifest.json` content as a UTF-8 string. Stored alongside `lakefile` so the image build is byte-deterministic: `lake update --keep-toolchain` resolves against this pinned manifest rather than the live registry. Mirrors the role `Manifest.toml` plays in the Julia runtime.

A reusable Lean library distinct from a `LeanProject` — typically a handler-side package baked into a `LeanEnvironment.included_packages` alongside the worker's own project. Same `lakefile` + `lake_manifest` shape as `LeanProject`; the distinction is semantic (project = proof source; package = supporting library) and surfaces in dispatch policy (the worker invokes `lean_export` only against `LeanProject` resources). Both subclasses of `RuntimePackage` so the substrate's chain-walk treats them uniformly when staging the build context.

Parsed Eigon view of one entry in a Lean `lake-manifest.json` — a single pinned dependency (Git URL + rev + package name). Inherits the `RuntimePackagePin` shape; the parsed projection lets EigenQL queries (`find every LeanEnvironment depending on Mathlib pinned at rev X`) work without re-parsing the manifest at query time. Optional in 20a.5a — emitted by the substrate's `lake_manifest_parse` helper landing in 20a.5b once a query consumer is written.

The unit of pinned Lean-side reproducibility (D26 §5.3 specialised for Lean). References the toolchain version, the Lake-resolved manifest hash, an axiom allowlist applied during nanoda re-verification, and a hard-error policy for unpermitted axioms. The image digest pinned on the underlying `RuntimeEnvironment` covers the toolchain bits; the axiom-allowlist + lockfile-hash fields here pin the policy bits that aren't in the OCI image digest's input set.

Allowlist of Lean axiom names accepted by every nanoda verification dispatched against proofs produced from this environment. Defaults to Lean's four trust-the-compiler axioms (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, `Lean.trustCompiler`) per D28 §7.1. Tighter allowlists (e.g. constructive-only deployments excluding `Classical.choice`) are an explicit policy decision; the orchestrator's env-create path stamps the default unless the user opts out.

Whether encountering an axiom outside `lean_permitted_axioms` produces a hard verification error (`true`) or silent skipping (`false`). Mirrors nanoda's `Config.unpermitted_axiom_hard_error`. Defaults to `true` — silent skipping is a footgun for audit chains, but the policy is explicit so deployments handling third-party Lean code (e.g. mining axiom dependencies from imports) can opt out at the LeanEnvironment level rather than monkey-patching the verification path.

SHA-256 hex digest of the `lake-manifest.json` baked into the `LeanEnvironment` image. Captured separately from the OCI image digest so a query can verify the lockfile didn't drift between image build and dispatch time without unpacking the image — the lockfile pin is the determinism anchor on the Lean dependency side, parallel to how the toolchain version pins the runtime side.

Fully-qualified Lean module name (e.g. `TestProject.Foo` or `Mathlib.Topology.Basic`). Carried on the `target_module` input Resource to the `lean_export` worker verb — the dispatch ships every call_method input as an Eigon-CBOR Resource and the Lake worker reads this property to know which module to dump via `lake exe lean4export`.

Unqualified Lean declaration name (e.g. `foo`, `add_zero`). Carried on the `target_constant` input Resource to the `lean_export` worker verb — pinning a single constant keeps the export bounded (otherwise `lake exe lean4export <Module>` dumps the entire transitive imported environment, which is hundreds of MB for any project importing Lean stdlib).
